entities.summary: Joseph-Norbert Provencher (unknown-1853) was a key figure in the founding of the modern province of Manitoba, Canada. As the first Bishop of Saint Boniface, he played a crucial role in the history of the Franco-Manitoban community, working to establish a strong Catholic presence in the region. His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to shape the province's cultural identity and lay the groundwork for future generations of Manitobans. Provencher's commitment to education and missionary work had a lasting impact on the community, as he established several schools and churches, including the iconic St. Boniface Cathedral. Today, he is remembered as a champion of French-Canadian culture and a pioneer in the history of Manitoba.
